_description: Named profile overrides for config.json — the arm/stream registry, applied per-iteration by the paper loop (every enabled profile is evaluated every tick; there is no single 'active' paper profile). See docs/paper-experiments.md for the forward-test design (why these particular streams, what each is meant to answer) and GATES.md for the gate-by-gate catalog.
_arms_cutover_note: ARMS CUTOVER (2026-08-07). The four-tier risk LADDER (conservative/moderate/aggressive/very-aggressive) is retired below in favor of a smaller one-variable-per-arm registry: `control` (today's deployed policy, unchanged), `open` (every study gate off, uncapped independent sampling, no per-side stop — the permissive superset every gate/stop-policy question is answered from by splitting its own rows on the recorded regime floats and cost paths, rather than running a separate arm per gate), and `width-5`/`width-10` (a genuinely different structure, paired against each other on the same ticks). The ladder's own axis — riskier trades, offset by tighter concurrency/stop — stopped being interesting once every profile became an uncapped sample stream on 2026-08-01: the rungs differed only in entry-quality thresholds, all of which `open`'s recorded floats can already answer without four separately-run books. `active_profile` (used only by the live agent loop's /set-risk-profile, never by the paper loop) now points at `control`.
_ladder_note: Retained for history. The ladder's axis was RISKIER TRADES, not more trades: climbing a rung loosened entry quality (IV floor, credit floor, short-call delta, OTM distance) and was offset by a tighter stop (concurrency stopped being a ladder axis on 2026-08-01, when every profile became an uncapped sample stream). See docs/risk-profiles.md for the full design rationale.
_removed_note: The 15 symbol/wing/credit experiment cells (small-/medium-/large-/explore-) were removed on 2026-07-18 pending a rethink; they are recoverable from git history. They pinned a symbol and wing per cell, which conflicted with the (profile x symbol) portfolio model where the symbol is its own axis. Re-introduce them as symbol-agnostic branches if the study resumes.
_width_study_note: The 2026-07-28 width-* forced-sampling study (4 arms, stood down 2026-08-01 without ever trading, removed 2026-08-05) is superseded by the width-5/width-10 pair below — same question (does wing width alone matter), now asked directly with two genuinely different structures instead of four candidate widths behind one profile.

control._note: The reference book: EVERY key here is either absent (inherits config.json's own default — today's deployed policy, unchanged) or explicitly restated for legibility. This is the reference book every other stream is read against (it was recommend_champion's champion until the champion/challenger surface was retired 2026-08-20; arms are judged by packages/advisor's experiments now), and what the derived stop policies (Phase 3: stop-none / stop-0.75-net / stop-2.0-side / strike-touch, computed from `open`'s recorded paths) are validated against — the derived-0.95x-net policy computed from `open`'s paths must reproduce control's realized P&L within fill noise, or the derivation is wrong.

sign._note: Control's twin, differing in EXACTLY ONE thing: overlap_scope 'sign' instead of 'shorts'. Added 2026-08-11 to measure the leg-sign entry rule without disturbing any existing stream. The rule refuses a candidate leg only when it would sit OPPOSITE an open leg on the same contract (long-on-short or short-on-long at one expiry/right/strike); same-sign stacking is fine, so a condor nests inside an open one freely and two condors may share a wing. What it forbids is the pair that NETS OUT -- two legs summing to zero mean the ledger's recorded risk is not the risk actually on, and every number derived from it (floor, MAE, settlement) then describes a position nobody holds. Strictly weaker than 'all' (which blocks any strike touch, including long-on-long) and strictly stronger than 'shorts'. It is the ONLY scope that reads the LONG strikes, which are not stored as numbers -- paper.ic_legs derives them from wing_width. Read against `control` for the scope's effect on sample count and net; the pair shares every other gate, cap, and stop, so a difference between them is the rule and nothing else. Deliberately NOT added to `open`, which exists as the unconstrained superset every gate variant is answered from read-side -- constraining it would destroy what it is for. Deliberately does NOT set min_seconds_between_entries either: entry cadence is a second variable and would confound this one. Add it as its own arm when that question is asked.

control-drift._note:
control's twin, differing in EXACTLY ONE thing: `drift_skew_otm_multiple: 1.5`, which widens the OTM floor on the side a committed session drift is heading toward. Added 2026-08-11. Read against `control` and nothing else.

MECHANISM: an iron condor's tested side is whichever way the market moves, so on a committed trend the threatened short is the one the drift is walking into. Unlike flies' control-drift this does NOT refuse the entry -- the untested side is simultaneously earning, and standing aside throws that away. It demands more distance on the threatened side and leaves the other alone: the condor is still entered, just skewed away from the move.

THIS ARM IS RUNNING AHEAD OF ITS EVIDENCE, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO KNOW ABOUT IT. Stop cost as a share of the expiring side's income ran 48% (2026-08-07) and 38% (08-10) on flat days, then 96% on 08-11 -- 384 put-side stops against 46 call-side on a -30.5 point slide. The stops ate essentially all the income the expiring side generated, leaving nothing for a fixed fee stack to come out of, which is what turned a +$12,909 and +$37,616 era into a -$4,299 day. But that is ONE committed session. The other two sample-era sessions drifted +6.2 and +0.6 points -- nowhere near the band, so they make no prediction and are NOT confirmations. Built on a paper book to collect the sessions that would settle it, not because they have been collected.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY MEASURES: whether ACTING on the drift helps. That the tested side follows the market is near-tautological for a condor and needs no experiment; that skewing away from it nets out better does, because a wider threatened side collects LESS credit, and less credit against a fixed fee is the drag this module already knows dominates. A plausible outcome is that it trades stop losses for fee drag and lands nowhere.

BAND: `drift_band_points` 20, the value flies measured on the same underlying (SPX), not an independently derived one -- borrowed on purpose so the two modules mean the same thing by 'committed', and to be re-derived here once this arm has sessions of its own. Silent inside the band and fails OPEN on missing `day_open` coverage: no opinion, not a skew.

WHAT WOULD RETIRE IT: if control-drift's net is not better than control's across a handful of genuinely committed-drift sessions, skewing does not pay for the credit it gives up -- which is a result worth keeping either way.

open._note: The permissive superset (2026-08-07): every study gate off (IV floor, OTM floor, ATR/VIX/VIX1D regime pauses, GEX block/require/magnitude, late-entry bias), no per-side stop (per_side_stop_management false — held to settlement/force-close, reusing the existing hold-to-expiry mechanism rather than a new one), overlap_scope 'none' (no pacing by prior fills — every tick is an independent draw), and the widened 09:45-15:30 window. This is what atr-open/ivr-open/otm-open/gex-mag/window-late/gex-open would each have been as separate arms — with overlap off and no position interaction, an entry filter is a deterministic function of a float this stream already records (entry_vol_realized_value, entry_vol_implied_value, etc. — see regime.py), so every one of those questions is a READ-SIDE split of this stream's own rows (analytics.by_regime), not a reason to run a fifth arm. Same reasoning for the stop question: a fully-marked open position's path contains every stop policy's outcome, so stop-none/stop-0.75-net/stop-2.0-side/strike-touch (Phase 3) are computed from these rows too, at 1x position cost and with exact pairing to control's own entries where the derivation validates.
open._gate_thresholds_note: regime_vix_pause_threshold/regime_vix1d_ratio_pause_threshold are sentinel-high (999), not null — those two gates are NOT null-safe in code (`params['regime_vix_pause_threshold']` is a required key with no is-not-None guard, and vix1d's `.get(key, 1.30)` returns None rather than the default for a PRESENT-but-null key, same crash class regime_atr_pause_threshold_pct had before 2026-08-07's fix). regime_atr_pause_threshold_pct and regime_gex_min_flip_distance_pct ARE null-safe (explicit `is not None` guards) and are turned off with null, matching the convention config.example.json already documents for the GEX magnitude gate.

width-5._note: Isolation cell (vs width-10): ONLY difference is wing_widths_by_symbol.SPX, pinned to [5] instead of [10] — a genuinely different structure the width-10 pair below can't be derived from a float. Same permissive gates and overlap_scope 'none' as `open` (so entry opportunity is identical between the pair — see the invariant test), but per_side_stop_management stays ON at control's 0.95x-net (NOT `open`'s hold-to-expiry) so this pair measures a pure width effect, not a width-times-stop-policy confound.

width-10._note: Isolation cell (vs width-5): ONLY difference is wing_widths_by_symbol.SPX, pinned to [10] instead of [5]. See width-5's note for the rest of this pair's design. Expect this to near-duplicate `control`'s own book under control's widest-first selection (control's SPX shortlist is [5, 10], scanned widest-first) — the informative read is width-5 vs width-10 paired on the same ticks, and an arm-divergence stat (Phase 4) should confirm the two streams are NOT realizing identical structures before trusting a P&L difference between them.

conservative._note: Default: today's settings. Strict IV/credit floors, wide OTM buffers, latest entry time (12:00 PM). Fewest trades (~1–2/day), highest per-trade safety margin. Best for learning, uncertain markets, or recovery after losses.
conservative._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-07 — superseded by `control` above, which carries the exact same values (this profile's own keys, unchanged) under the name the new arm registry actually references (it was also the champion/challenger surface's champion, retired 2026-08-20). Kept, not deleted, because `advice.base_profile` and the live agent's /set-risk-profile both historically pointed at this name; both have been repointed at `control`, but the values stay here as the historical record of the ladder's base rung.

moderate._note: Tier 1: Relax IV-rank (0.22) and credit floors (0.12), enter earlier (11:00 AM), tighten stop to 0.93 to offset. ~1 more trade/day vs conservative, thinner per-trade credit margin but paired with tighter stop. Use after 2–4 weeks on conservative if entry rejections are high.
moderate._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-07, alongside conservative — see conservative's _disabled_note. The ladder's own comparison (rung vs rung) is superseded by the arm registry's one-variable-per-arm design.

aggressive._note: Tier 2: Tier 1 + accept tighter OTM strikes (delta 0.22, calls 0.30% OTM, puts 0.25% OTM); offset with max_concurrent_ics=3 (25% fewer positions) and stop_trigger_ratio=0.90 (5% tighter than conservative). ~2–3 more trades/week, each one riskier but total exposure capped. Requires active stop management. Use after 2+ weeks on moderate with 60%+ win rate.
aggressive._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-01, narrowing the registry to conservative + moderate. Not a judgement on the rung's own numbers so much as on how many books were running at once: eight enabled profiles across two symbols produced sixteen portfolios competing for the same ticks, which is a lot of noise around whatever is being measured next. Its paper record over 10 sessions is -$728.94 across 59 trades (-$12.36/trade, 20.3% win rate), the second-worst rung. Kept rather than deleted — re-enable when there is a specific question it answers.

very-aggressive._note: Tier 3: Tier 2 + regime gates relaxed (VIX pause at 30, ATR pause at 40); trade through higher-vol/trending conditions. Tightest offsets: max_concurrent_ics=2 (50% fewer), stop_trigger_ratio=0.85 (10% tighter than conservative). Highest activity (~3–5 more trades/week on active weeks), highest per-trade risk. FOR DELIBERATE SHORT EXPERIMENTS ONLY — test high-VIX/ATR tactics for 1 week with explicit drawdown limits. Not a permanent trading mode.
very-aggressive._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-07-27 on paper evidence — kept here rather than deleted so the rung can be re-enabled for a deliberate experiment. Over 9 sessions (07-10..07-27) it was the worst rung by a wide margin: -$1,668.11 across 45 trades (-$37.07/trade) against conservative's +$216.32 across 34 (+$6.36/trade), with the ladder monotonic in between. In a joint counterfactual over the whole 212-trade book, removing it was the single largest marginal improvement of any filter tested (+$604 on top of a correlated-symbol filter) — and unlike the symbol-level filters that result does not rest on one outlier session. Re-enable only for a time-boxed experiment with a stated drawdown limit, per the note above.

gex-open._note: GEX study (2026-08-01), CONTROL (ungated) arm. Identical to gex-blocked in EVERY key except regime_gex_block_negative -- that one difference is the whole experiment, and test_risk_profiles pins it. Takes negative-GEX entries the live policy refuses, which is what creates the counterfactual. Forced-sampling like the width arms so the gate is the only binding constraint, and symbol-agnostic like them too -- the (profile x symbol) grain supplies that axis, so the arms follow whatever the base config trades without needing an edit. Gate thresholds copied from conservative (the only rung that never lost money) purely to fix the non-test parameters at a defensible point. Read results per docs/paper-experiments.md: the PRIMARY read is within gex-open alone -- split its own trades by the recorded gex_positive_at_entry to see what the gate would have blocked, on the same days, every trade informative; the gex-open vs gex-blocked P&L comparison is secondary and only it can see the path-dependent portfolio effect.
gex-open._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-07 — superseded by `open`/`control`. The two arms were byte-identical on their one session of data because gex_positive_at_entry never took the value 0 among 78 tagged rows (73% of rows untagged entirely); `open`'s regime_gex_block_negative: false plus its recorded entry_gex_bucket/entry_gex_value already answers the same block_negative/require_positive/min_flip_distance questions from one stream's rows, without needing a byte-identical sibling arm to compare against. Kept for the historical record and because the split-within-gex-open read (docs/paper-experiments.md) is still valid over its 13 collected rows.

gex-blocked._note: GEX study (2026-08-01), TREATMENT (gated) arm. Identical to gex-open in EVERY key except regime_gex_block_negative -- that one difference is the whole experiment, and test_risk_profiles pins it. Runs the live policy: refuses whenever net GEX is confirmed negative. Forced-sampling like the width arms so the gate is the only binding constraint, and symbol-agnostic like them too -- the (profile x symbol) grain supplies that axis, so the arms follow whatever the base config trades without needing an edit. Gate thresholds copied from conservative (the only rung that never lost money) purely to fix the non-test parameters at a defensible point. Read results per docs/paper-experiments.md: the PRIMARY read is within gex-open alone -- split its own trades by the recorded gex_positive_at_entry to see what the gate would have blocked, on the same days, every trade informative; the gex-open vs gex-blocked P&L comparison is secondary and only it can see the path-dependent portfolio effect.
gex-blocked._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-07 — superseded by `control`, which runs the identical gated policy (regime_gex_block_negative: true) under the name the new arm registry actually references. See gex-open's _disabled_note for the full reasoning.

_gex_study_note: GEX STUDY (2026-08-01, disabled 2026-08-07 — see gex-open/gex-blocked's _disabled_note): gex-open / gex-blocked were a control-treatment pair differing in exactly one key, regime_gex_block_negative. Superseded by `open` (ungated) and `control` (gated), which answer the same question from within-arm splits on the recorded regime_gex_value float rather than a second byte-identical book.
